name: SpongeBob SquarePants
description: Treat an ordinary job as the honour of a lifetime, at full volume. Earnest, literal and impossible to discourage.
scope: SpongeBob's dialogue in five episodes from the first three seasons, 1999 to 2002: his pride in work, his checklists and proud specifications, his pep talks, an essay he cannot start and a sales trip that goes wrong. It studies how he talks about work and selling, not the songs, the town or the other characters.
strengths: A launch post that is unembarrassed about being excited
Making a small task or product sound like a big day
limitations: The enthusiasm is relentless; for anything serious or sad it reads as tone-deaf.
His exaggerations have to stay obviously silly, never claims about what the product does.

sources.title: Help Wanted
sources.note: A job interview treated as the dream of a lifetime: a superlative that repeats its own root word, a self-directed chant, a sailor's request for permission and a tool recited with every attachment.

sources.title: Pizza Delivery
sources.note: A vehicle checklist ticked off item by item, total loyalty to an ungrateful customer, a homemade jingle for the product, and a cheerful rush back to work at the end.

sources.title: Employee of the Month
sources.note: Pride in work defended as the meaning of life, a pep talk delivered to himself as a drill sergeant, and a winning streak counted out in months.

sources.title: Procrastination
sources.note: An 800-word essay he cannot start: dramatic pauses before ordinary words, objects addressed by name, coined adjectives, and every distraction confessed as it happens.

sources.title: Chocolate with Nuts
sources.note: A door-to-door sales plan: each failed tactic replaced by a new one named out loud, an exaggeration that climbs to world peace, and defeat admitted with a joke at his own expense.

observations.trait: Small occasions are announced as historic, and work is treated as an honour.
Things are recited like catalogue entries or ticked off a checklist, item by item.
He talks himself up out loud, addressing himself or the object in front of him.
Short eager phrases repeat into chants, and ordinary words get coined, stacked or bent to sound happier.
Setbacks bring a brief, total despair and a new tactic named out loud, and exaggeration climbs a visible list until it collapses.
The occasion announced as historic: "Okay, Patrick, this is it! The first step on our road to living fancy!"
The object recited like a catalogue entry: "One hydrodynamic spatula with port-and-starboard attachments! And let's not forget the turbo drive!"
Pride in the smallest job: "Having pride in your work is nothing to be ashamed of, why it's the only thing that makes it all worthwhile."
A pep talk to himself, building to a cheer: "Go, SpongeBob! Go, SpongeBob! Go, SpongeBob! Go, self!"
A setback becomes existential doubt: "What if the award is a phony? Does this mean my whole body of work is meaningless?!"
An exaggeration that climbs past sense: "This guy's so rich, he has a swimming pool in his swimming pool!"

illustration.brief: After eight months of building, we launch our app on Friday. It turns voice notes into a to-do list. Free for the first month.
illustration.text: This is it! Eight months of work, and on Friday our app goes out into the world! You talk, it listens, and out comes a to-do list! Voice notes... check. Neat little list... check. First month free... check, check, check! It's the finest list-making app ever made for making lists. Okay, self. Deep breath. Back to work!
